extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and usage rules for writing news articles and copy to Reuters editorial standards, covering word choice, capitalization, punctuation, units, national/organizational names, and other stylistic and factual conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: move to
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid saying 'moved to' when the only action was verbal; the phrase can give a spurious sense of physical action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Do not write 'Clinton moved to head off congressional opposition...' when he only spoke; use a more precise alternative describing the verbal action.

rubrics_metrics.name: mpg, mph
rubrics_metrics.description: Use abbreviations 'mpg' and 'mph' in second and subsequent references; spell out in full on first reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both abbreviations lower case and without full stops. Spell out 'miles per gallon' and 'miles per hour' on first reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ms
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use the title 'Ms' in Reuters style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use Ms; also avoid Mr, Mrs, Miss, Master as listed (note: context suggests preferred forms are other courtesy titles or none).

rubrics_metrics.name: Muhammad
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred spelling is 'Mohammad'.

rubrics_metrics.name: mujahideen
rubrics_metrics.description: Term denotes Islamic guerrilla groups; means 'holy warriors'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as descriptive term but be aware of connotations; entry defines meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mullah
rubrics_metrics.description: A Muslim scholar; usage varies by country and can be pejorative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using 'mullah' in an Iranian context and never use it as shorthand for Tehran’s religious-political leadership unless quoting someone. In Afghanistan it is a neutral term for prayer leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: multi- prefix
rubrics_metrics.description: Words starting with 'multi' are not hyphenated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: multilateral, multinational, multicultural, multilingual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mumbai
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Mumbai' not 'Bombay' except in proper names.

rubrics_metrics.name: murder
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'murder' only for violent deaths without political overtones and generally avoid unless there has been a conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Otherwise use 'killing' unless 'murder' is part of a criminal charge or trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Murphy's law
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the phrase; it means 'if something can go wrong, it will'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only explain it if it appears in a quote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Muslim spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Muslim', not 'Moslem'.

rubrics_metrics.name: mute
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'mute' for someone physically unable to speak; avoid 'dumb'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer 'speech impaired' for people who have difficulty speaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Myanmar
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Myanmar' (formerly Burma).

rubrics_metrics.name: NAACP
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell out: National Association for the Advancement of Colored Peoples (U.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: NAFTA
rubrics_metrics.description: North American Free Trade Agreement — trade pact between U.S., Mexico and Canada.

rubrics_metrics.name: names (cross-ref)
rubrics_metrics.description: See entries for personal names, proper names, courtesy titles, nobility, religious titles, royalty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nanjing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Nanjing' not 'Nanking'.

rubrics_metrics.name: nano- prefix
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefix meaning one-billionth of a unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: naphtha
rubrics_metrics.description: Spell 'naphtha' (not 'naptha').

rubrics_metrics.name: NASA
rubrics_metrics.description: National Aeronautics and Space Administration (U.S.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At first reference 'the U.S. space agency NASA' is acceptable. See www.nasa.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: nation (avoid generic 'the nation’s')
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not write 'the nation’s' when referring to a specific country; be specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: use 'Britain’s largest airport' or 'Germany’s largest airport' rather than 'the nation’s capital'. Avoid American cliché 'the nation’s capital' for Washington; use 'the U.S. capital'.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Guard
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain to international readers that in the U.S. it is a militia force; capitalization rules differ by country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In American style, capitalize for U.S. or state forces ('the National Guard', 'Kansas National Guard'). Lower case for national guards of other countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: national names (dateline nationality omission)
rubrics_metrics.description: You need not specify a minister’s nationality in the lead if the story has a dateline in that country; same for groups obviously of that dateline nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: under a Washington dateline write 'Secretary of State Joan Smith said...' not 'U.S. Secretary of State...'. Under an Athens dateline write 'Police arrested' not 'Greek police arrested'.

rubrics_metrics.name: nationalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Write nationalities in full and do not abbreviate in stories and sports results (except 'U.S.' for United States).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Britain' and 'British' (not 'United Kingdom' or 'Great Britain'). Use 'The Netherlands' (not 'Holland') and 'Taiwan' (not 'Chinese Taipei'). Distinguish between North and South Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: national security adviser
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower case; not an official title.

rubrics_metrics.name: nationwide
rubrics_metrics.description: Rarely necessary; avoid 'nationwide broadcast' unless specifying if it is not nationwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a head of state/government goes on TV or radio, assume the broadcast is nationwide; specify only if it is not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native American
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred term; includes Inuit and others; 'American Indian' acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible be more specific and give tribal name, e.g. Navajo, Cherokee. See race entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: NATO
rubrics_metrics.description: North Atlantic Treaty Organization (Brussels). Initials may be used at first reference with full name given lower in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: www.nato.int.

rubrics_metrics.name: naught, nought
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'naught' in phrases like 'you come to naught' or 'set a naught'; 'nought' is the number zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: nauseous vs nauseated
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Nauseous' means causing nausea; 'nauseated' means sickened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only very objectionable people are 'nauseous'; ordinary people are 'nauseated'.

rubrics_metrics.name: nautical mile
rubrics_metrics.description: One nautical mile = 1,852 metres or 1.1515 statute miles; do not convert nautical miles used for fishing limits, by ships, NASA reports, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using nautical miles in space stories make this clear in text. See also 'knot'.

rubrics_metrics.name: naval vs navel
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Naval' pertains to warships or a navy; 'navel' is the centre of the abdomen.

rubrics_metrics.name: nave, knave
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Nave' is main part of a church; 'knave' is a deceitful person.

rubrics_metrics.name: navy capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: International style: capitalize when part of formal title (the British Navy, the Royal Navy), otherwise lower case; American style: capitalize for U.S. Navy, lower case for other navies.

rubrics_metrics.name: nearby vs near by
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Nearby' is an adjective (the nearby town). 'Near by' is an adverb (we stayed near by).

rubrics_metrics.name: negatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid awkward negatives and constructions with 'not'; prefer positive or alternative phrasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'decided against' instead of 'decided not to'; 'unnecessary' instead of 'not necessary'; 'declined to comment' instead of 'would not comment'. Avoid officialese euphemisms with 'negative' (e.g. 'negative growth' → 'shrinking').

rubrics_metrics.name: neither, nor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'neither ... nor' to govern only two elements; verb agreement rules depend on nearest noun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not write 'neither...or' or use 'not...nor'; use 'not...or'. Examples provided for singular/plural agreement and mixed-number agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPAD
rubrics_metrics.description: New Partnership for Africa’s Development (Midrand, South Africa); agency to strengthen governance and mobilize finance for Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See www.nepad.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nepali
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Nepali' not 'Nepalese' as adjective.

rubrics_metrics.name: nerve-racking
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry title present but content not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Netherlands
rubrics_metrics.description: In text write 'the Netherlands'; in datelines omit the article (e.g. ARNHEM, Netherlands, May 16).

rubrics_metrics.name: nevertheless
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry title present but guidance not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: new (often redundant)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'New' is often superfluous; companies announcing a plant already imply it will be new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omit 'new' when unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: news conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'news conference' to 'press conference'.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Year's Eve/Day
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize 'New Year’s Eve' and 'New Year’s Day'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also 'but good luck in the new year' (example of lowercase use when generic).

rubrics_metrics.name: newspaper titles capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not capitalise articles and particles in English-language newspaper/magazine names contrary to masthead style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the New York Times, the News of the World. For some non-English newspapers that begin with 'the', write 'O Globo/Le Monde/Die Welt' (no leading 'the' when using the foreign masthead word).

rubrics_metrics.name: nicknames
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a person's preferred nickname instead of given name if that's their preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Tiger Woods.

rubrics_metrics.name: nighttime
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; content not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nissan, Nissen
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Nissan cars', 'Nissen hut'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nobel Prize
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Nobel Prize' and plural 'Nobel Prizes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: noisome vs noisy
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Noisome' means disgusting to sight or smell; 'noisy' offends hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not confuse the terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: no man’s land
rubrics_metrics.description: Write 'no man’s land' (not 'no-man’s-land').

rubrics_metrics.name: no one
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'no one' not 'noone' or 'no-one'.

rubrics_metrics.name: nobility
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains British hereditary and life peerage titles, forms of address and second-reference usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed rules: use full title at first reference for dukes, then surname/territorial name at second reference; refer to other peers as 'Lord So-and-So' and wives as 'Lady So-and-So'; baronets/knights as 'Sir'; dames as 'Dame'; do not use 'Hon.' for untitled sons of peers. Use given name and surname for well-known life peers at first reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: non- prefix hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenate when the first element of a word is the negative 'non-'; otherwise compound may be closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'non-aggression pact' but 'nonconformist'.

rubrics_metrics.name: none
rubrics_metrics.description: As the subject, 'none' may be followed by either singular or plural verb.

rubrics_metrics.name: nonetheless
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; guidance not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nordic countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Nordic countries (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden) and clarify 'Scandinavia' (Denmark, Norway, Sweden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of potential confusion, list countries even if using 'Nordic' or 'Scandinavia' in a lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalcy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'normality' instead of 'normalcy'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Northern Ireland
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Northern' is always upper case; avoid 'Ulster' except in quotes; guidance on describing the IRA and related terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IRA initials at first reference; do not describe IRA as a 'Catholic group'; describe Sinn Fein as political ally of the IRA; avoid 'paramilitary' and use more specific terms like 'guerrillas, gunmen or bombers' depending on context; avoid 'loyalists' for Protestant guerrillas unless quoting.

rubrics_metrics.name: notable
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'notable' (not 'noteable').

rubrics_metrics.name: noted
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'noted' only for established facts, not for claims or opinions; avoid overuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: now
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'now' instead of flabby phrases like 'at the present time' or 'at this time'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Now' is strong and simple.

rubrics_metrics.name: nowadays
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; guidance not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: nuclear power glossary
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines frequently used nuclear terms (becquerel, criticality, curie, fission, fusion, half-life, meltdown, plutonium, rad, radiation/radioactivity, roentgen, sievert, uranium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides unit conversions, definitions and reporting guidance (e.g., be cautious with conversions and context such as fishing limits or space shots). Use appropriate units and explain very small/large quantities (e.g., becquerel units may be in trillions).

rubrics_metrics.name: numbers (cross-ref)
rubrics_metrics.description: See entries for figures and fractions (not expanded in chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: numerous
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'many' as shorter, better alternative to 'numerous'.

rubrics_metrics.name: numskull
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct spelling is 'numbskull' (not 'numskull').

rubrics_metrics.name: OAPEC
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (Kuwait). Note American spelling 'Organization'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up in 1968; aims to improve economic co-operation in petroleum industry; members listed; group normally does not make decisions on oil output or pricing. See www.oapecorg.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: OAS
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization of American States (Washington); 35 active members representing Americas except Cuba (non-active member).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See http://www.oas.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: oasis, oases
rubrics_metrics.description: Pluralization guidance (entry listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: OAU
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisation of African Unity (Addis Ababa) — superseded by African Union.

rubrics_metrics.name: obscenities
rubrics_metrics.description: Use obscene language only if in direct quotes and if the story would be seriously weakened by omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If retained, do not euphemise with dots. Generally avoid quoting mindless obscenities from ordinary people, athletes or soldiers; consider using them if prominent public figures use them in context that affects fitness for office or emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: obsolescent, obsolete
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Obsolescent' means on the way to becoming 'obsolete'.

rubrics_metrics.name: occur, occurring, occurred
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; guidance not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: ocean capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower case when used alone or in plurals (e.g., Indian and Pacific oceans). Capitalize named oceans: Antarctic Ocean, Arctic Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Pacific Ocean.

rubrics_metrics.name: octopuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Plural 'octopuses' preferred; not 'octopi'.

rubrics_metrics.name: OECD
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development; OECD itself uses a hyphen in its formal name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Established in 1961; gives economic advice to members and non-members. See http://www.oecd.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: of/of the (can be excised)
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'of' or 'of the' can often be removed for brevity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'the centre of the town' → 'the town centre'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-spinner
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenated for a type of bowler in cricket.

rubrics_metrics.name: official titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Be restrained in using idiomatic phrases to describe officials or bodies instead of official titles; idioms should be used sparingly and official title given in the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pejorative idioms like 'trade union boss'. Use idioms when necessary in leads but give the official title later.

rubrics_metrics.name: officials (term usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not describe government ministers as 'officials'.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIC
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisation of the Islamic Conference; principal world organisation of Muslim states with 57 members; funded mainly by Saudi Arabia and based in Jeddah.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See www.oic-oci.org. Note related institutions like the Islamic Development Bank.

rubrics_metrics.name: oil barrels (conversion)
rubrics_metrics.description: One barrel = 35 Imperial or 42 U.S. gallons = 159 litres = 0.159 cubic metres; conversions to tonnes depend on specific gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide example conversion factors: Brent crude multiply by 7.57 to get tonnes per barrel; WTI has 7.62 barrels per tonne; Urals 7.33. Refined products vary; use typical conversion numbers given.

rubrics_metrics.name: oilfield
rubrics_metrics.description: One word ('oilfield').

rubrics_metrics.name: oil statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Express production/export figures in barrels per day (bpd) and standardize on bpd; if quoting tonnes per year give bpd as bracketed conversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When converting tonnes per year to bpd, divide barrel figure by 365 for daily rate. Give approximate conversions with no more decimal places than original figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: oil strikes
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not report 'discovery of a new oil well'—the phrase is incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correct concept is discovery of oil/gas, not a 'new oil well' ready-made.

rubrics_metrics.name: OK
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'OK' not 'okay'; avoid in alerts and headlines; do not use in text unless quoting.

rubrics_metrics.name: old-time, old-timer, old times
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenation as listed for these expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: oligopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: a few firms control supply and influence price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Olympiad
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Olympiad' only to mean the four-year period between Olympic Games.

rubrics_metrics.name: on behalf of
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'by' unless you really mean 'acting as a representative of' or 'in the interests of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: on to vs into
rubrics_metrics.description: 'On to' is two words; 'into' is one word.

rubrics_metrics.name: one word or two (hyphenation guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporary usage prefers one word; hyphenation is increasingly rare though use hyphen if it clarifies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid double consonants or vowels that detract from clarity. As a general rule words with 'pre-' and 'post-' prefixes should be one word. Use common sense; see further hyphenation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ongoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Usually tautological ('the ongoing crisis'); prefer 'continuing' or omit.

rubrics_metrics.name: online
rubrics_metrics.description: One word for computer connections and the Internet ('online').

rubrics_metrics.name: only (placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Only' should go immediately before the word or phrase it qualifies to avoid ambiguity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrating how placement changes meaning with SAS flight examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPEC
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (use 'Organization' spelling); acronym may be used at first reference with a descriptive tag; full title should be given at second reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not place the acronym in brackets immediately after full reference. It is permissible to call OPEC a 'cartel'. Use 'output ceiling/limit' rather than 'the OPEC quota' (singular). Members listed; see www.opec.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: opera titles
rubrics_metrics.description: See capitalization rules for titles (not expanded in chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: opinion polls (minimum info)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories based on opinion polls should include the organiser's name, who published it, sample size, and how/where it was carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If available, give margin of error and survey history (regularity). Do not base stories on Internet polls unless from reputable polling organisations. Avoid using the word 'poll' in headlines unless commissioned by Reuters.

rubrics_metrics.name: optimum
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Optimum' is not a simple superlative meaning 'biggest/best/largest'; it means best for achieving a specific aim or the point of most favourable condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: ordnance vs ordinance
rubrics_metrics.description: 'ordnance' = artillery; 'ordinance' = a decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: organisations and institutions (name style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the name style that appears on an organisation’s official website.

rubrics_metrics.name: orient
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'to orientate'; when referring to the Far East capitalise 'Oriental' in 'Oriental cuisine'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orthodox Church
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains Eastern Rite Churches and historic context (1054 East-West split) and reunion with Rome for some rites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives background on rites and reunification history; use appropriate capitalisation and descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Osama bin Laden
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'bin Laden' at second reference; refer to him as 'Saudi-born' after he was stripped of Saudi citizenship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oscars (Academy Awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Oscars' or 'Academy Awards' for the annual statuettes presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: others (avoid vagueness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware using 'others' in reporting figures like casualties; it is often unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: '50 people were killed and 200 others injured' — 'others' may be redundant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ottawa
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; likely usage as place name (not expanded here).

rubrics_metrics.name: ounce (conversions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To convert to grams roughly multiply by 30; precisely multiply by 28.35. Dry ounce = 28.35 g; troy ounce = 31.10 g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liquid/fluid ounce: UK = 28.4 ml (20 fl oz = 1 pint); US = 29.6 ml (16 fl oz = 1 pint).

rubrics_metrics.name: ouster
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside legal context, prefer 'ousting'; use 'dismissal' or 'overthrow' as better terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: out of court / out-of-court
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'out-of-court settlement' and phrase 'paid out of court'.

rubrics_metrics.name: outpatient
rubrics_metrics.description: One word ('outpatient').

rubrics_metrics.name: outside (phrase)
rubrics_metrics.description: Never use the phrase 'outside of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oval Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Oval Office' for the White House office of the president.

rubrics_metrics.name: over (use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'more than' with numbers (e.g., 'More than 100' instead of 'over 100').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep 'over' for place ('over the moon'). Do not use 'over' as 'because of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: overweening
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; content not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: oxford blue
rubrics_metrics.description: As a colour, lower case 'oxford blue'. If an athlete represented the University, use 'Oxford Blue'.

rubrics_metrics.name: oxymoron
rubrics_metrics.description: Define as figure of speech combining opposites, e.g., 'bitter-sweet', 'living dead'.

rubrics_metrics.name: paedophile vs pederast
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Paedophile' sexually desires children; 'pederast' has sexual relations with a boy.

rubrics_metrics.name: pail vs pale
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pail' = small bucket; 'pale' = wan or light in colour.

rubrics_metrics.name: palate, palette, pallet
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: 'palate' = sense of taste; 'palette' = artist's paint board; 'pallet' = mattress or small bed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Palestine Liberation Organisation' (not 'Palestinian'); 'PLO' acceptable on first reference and spelled out subsequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: pan prefix
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pan-' usually does not take a hyphen (panacea, panoply, pantheism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: 'Pan-American' hyphenated when referring to North/Central/South America region; official title of Pan America Games is not hyphenated. Also 'pan-African' and 'pan-European'.

rubrics_metrics.name: panacea
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: a universal medicine or cure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panchen Lama
rubrics_metrics.description: See related entries: Dalai Lama, Tibet (cross-reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panjsher
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred spelling 'Panjsher' (not Panjshar or Panjshir).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pap smear
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize 'Pap' (named after George Papanicolaou); a smear test for cancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: papal nuncio
rubrics_metrics.description: The Holy See’s ambassadors are called 'papal nuncios' and embassies 'nunciatures'; where no formal diplomatic relations exist the pope’s envoy is an 'apostolic delegate'.

rubrics_metrics.name: paparazzo, paparazzi
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide correct singular/plural (entry present but minimal content in chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: parallel, paralleling, paralleled
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; guidance not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: paraplegia
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: total or partial paralysis of both legs; 'quadriplegia' is paralysis of all four limbs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paris Club
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal body of creditor nations meeting in Paris to help indebted countries reorganize finances; treats debt for countries with IMF support and requires comparable terms from other lenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also 'loans', 'London Club'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parkinson's disease
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed (disease name capitalization guidance implicit).

rubrics_metrics.name: parliament (usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally refer to legislative assemblies as 'parliaments' initially, regardless of formal names; give formal name later in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Prime Minister Tony Blair told parliament ...' In American style capitalize when the name of a formal body (The British Parliament).

rubrics_metrics.name: parliamentarian
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Member of parliament' preferred though 'parliamentarian' is increasingly accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: part time vs part-time
rubrics_metrics.description: Two words for the verb ('to part time'), one word for the adjective ('part-time').

rubrics_metrics.name: partial or broken quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid partial or broken quotes unless the fragment is vital to understanding meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: participate
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'take part' to 'participate'.

rubrics_metrics.name: participles (dangling/unattached)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unattached participles can be acceptable when the sense is clear, but avoid when they make the sentence absurd or misattach the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided of acceptable and unacceptable usages; ensure subject clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: partner (relationship term)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'boyfriend, girlfriend or lover' instead of 'partner' in many contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pashtun spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Pashtun' (not Pushtun, Pushtoon, Pathan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes region and language (Pashto).

rubrics_metrics.name: passer-by, passers-by
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenation and pluralization guidance for 'passer-by'/'passers-by'.

rubrics_metrics.name: past vs last (usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usually mean 'last' when writing about time up to present; 'past' is vaguer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'injured for the last three games' not 'for the past three games'. Check for redundancy like 'past history'.

rubrics_metrics.name: passive voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid passive voice as it is longer, clumsier and often confuses the reader; use active voice where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examples: 'Police arrested five armed men' rather than 'Five armed men were arrested by police.' Passive is unavoidable when the subject of action is the main point (e.g., 'President Jane Flow was shot and killed by...').

rubrics_metrics.name: patrol, patrolling, patrolled
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; guidance not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: payroll
rubrics_metrics.description: One word (U.S. usage 'non-farm payrolls').

rubrics_metrics.name: peach Melba
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed (proper capitalization guidance for works of art/food names).

rubrics_metrics.name: peal, peel
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Peal of bells', 'orange peel'.

rubrics_metrics.name: pedal vs peddle
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pedal' = bicycle action; 'peddle' = sell goods. 'Pedaller' rides a bicycle; 'pedlar' sells goods; use 'drug peddler'.

rubrics_metrics.name: peer
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: an equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: pejorative
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; guidance not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: peninsular vs peninsula
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Peninsular' is the adjective; 'peninsula' is the noun. Example: 'The Peninsular War' was fought on the peninsula.

rubrics_metrics.name: per (avoid Latin)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid using 'per'; prefer 'each' (e.g., 'Six dollars each' not 'six dollars per item').

rubrics_metrics.name: percent
rubrics_metrics.description: One word; use numerals before 'percent' (4 percent). Use percent after both numbers when writing changes. Do not confuse percentage with percentage points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and calculation guidance provided. Use decimals not fractions in percentages and express to nearest two decimal places for complicated figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: percentage (word choice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'many' or 'most' rather than 'a large percentage of'.

rubrics_metrics.name: perceptible
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed; guidance not included in chunk.

rubrics_metrics.name: perfect
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not write 'more perfect' or 'less perfect'; things are either perfect or not. Use 'less than perfect'.

rubrics_metrics.name: period close quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods go inside quotation marks unless it's a broken quote, in which case they go outside.

rubrics_metrics.name: period of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Use either 'period' or 'time' but not both together (avoid 'period of time').

rubrics_metrics.name: perk
rubrics_metrics.description: Short for 'perquisite'; explain as a fringe benefit when used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persian (language name guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Persian' is the preferred overall name for the language spoken in Iran, Tajikistan and northern Afghanistan; local names include Farsi, Tajik, Dari.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persian Gulf
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Gulf' (context implies guidance to avoid 'Persian Gulf' contention).

rubrics_metrics.name: person vs people
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'person' for singular and 'people' for plural; do not use 'persons'.

rubrics_metrics.name: personal/personally/personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid redundant uses of 'personal/personally'; use 'people', 'staff' or 'workers' for 'personnel'.

rubrics_metrics.name: personal names (checking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check names repeatedly; use given name and surname at first reference and surname alone on second reference; use initials only if preferred by the individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clarity for unfamiliar names using gender pronouns where necessary. Be careful with variant spellings and consult author/source if inconsistent. See related national name entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: persuade vs convince
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Persuade' = get someone to do something; 'convince' = make someone believe something; never write 'convince to'.

rubrics_metrics.name: petrol bomb
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition: bottle of petrol with rag set alight on throwing; do not use 'Molotov cocktail'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petrodollar
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed (term usage in context of oil-related finance).

rubrics_metrics.name: PGA
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional Golfers’ Association (abbreviation guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: phase vs faze
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Phase' = stage; 'faze' = to worry/disturb.

rubrics_metrics.name: phenomenon vs phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Phenomenon' singular, 'phenomena' plural; do not use 'phenomenal' when meaning extraordinary or just large.

rubrics_metrics.name: phoney
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed (spelling guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: phosphorus
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed (term usage).

rubrics_metrics.name: picket, picketed, picket line
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed (word forms guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: picnic verb/noun forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms: picnic, picnicking, picknicked, picknicker (usage guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: pidgin English
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed (usage guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: pigeonhole
rubrics_metrics.description: Both noun and verb usage guidance (entry listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: pilots
rubrics_metrics.description: Military aircraft other than strategic bombers and transports normally carry one pilot; write 'the two crew' not 'the two pilots' when reporting incidents involving fighter-bombers with non-pilot crew.

rubrics_metrics.name: pileup
rubrics_metrics.description: One word as a noun, two words as a verb.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIN
rubrics_metrics.description: Stands for 'Personal Identification Number'; 'PIN number' is tautologous.

rubrics_metrics.name: pious
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid describing someone as 'a pious Muslim' or 'a pious Christian'; prefer 'practising'.

rubrics_metrics.name: plan ahead
rubrics_metrics.description: Use simply 'plan' rather than 'plan ahead'.

rubrics_metrics.name: plane vs plain
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'aircraft' for plane; 'higher plane' (not 'higher plain').

rubrics_metrics.name: planets capitalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize names of planets.

rubrics_metrics.name: plea bargain (noun/verb)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Plea bargain' is noun; 'plea-bargain' is verb (used intransitively).

rubrics_metrics.name: plead, pleading, pleaded
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'pleaded' not 'pled'; prefer legal usage 'pleaded'.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLO (again)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'PLO' on first reference and spell out subsequently; prefer 'Palestine Liberation Organisation'.

rubrics_metrics.name: plough vs plow
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Plough' British spelling; American style 'plow'.

rubrics_metrics.name: plummet
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'plummet' in market reports unless decline is precipitous; a 2-percent fall is not a plummet.

rubrics_metrics.name: plurality
rubrics_metrics.description: See 'majority, plurality' (cross-ref).

rubrics_metrics.name: p.m. (time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Format times as e.g. '3 p.m.' or '3:45 p.m.'

rubrics_metrics.name: podcast
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry listed (term usage guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: podium vs lectern/dais
rubrics_metrics.description: A speaker stands behind a lectern (stand for notes) on a podium; several speakers fit on a dais/rostrum/platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: poems (title capitalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalize every word in the title of poems apart from conjunctions, articles, particles and short prepositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The Rime of the Ancient Mariner', 'Elegy in a Country Churchyard', 'The Waste Land'.

rubrics_metrics.name: point-blank
rubrics_metrics.description: Note hyphenation for 'point-blank'.

rubrics_metrics.name: pointed out (avoid in contentious contexts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid 'pointed out' if statement is contentious because it suggests the writer accepts the speaker's claim; use 'said' instead.
